answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a stake that only grows slowly, like a sparrow earning trust one small flight at a time, while a Sybil swarm must pay the full bond for every clone. The bond is slashed on proven misbehavior, so an attacker who plants a ridge of fake accounts watches the whole ridge collapse at once; the nectar of cheap identities turns bitter because a thousand credible agents cost a thousand real stakes, not one copied key.
